record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: For the real two-dimensional space ℓ_p^2 with 1 < p < ∞, determine whether its numerical index equals sup_{t∈[0,1]} |t^{p-1} - t| / (1 + t^p).

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Is it true that, in the real case, n(ℓ2p) = sup t∈[0,1] |t^{p−1} − t| / (1 + t^p) for every 1 < p < ∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1<p<\infty$ and consider the real two-dimensional Banach space $\ell_p^2 = (\mathbb{R}^2, \|\cdot\|_p)$, where $\|(x_1,x_2)\|_p = (|x_1|^p + |x_2|^p)^{1/p}$. For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a real Banach space $X$, define the numerical radius
$$v(T) = \sup\{|x^*(Tx)| : x \in X,\ x^* \in X^*,\ \|x\|=\|x^*\|=x^*(x)=1\},$$
and the numerical index of $X$ by
$$n(X) = \inf\{v(T) : T \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \|T\|=1\}.$$
Equivalently, $n(X)$ is the largest constant $k \ge 0$ such that $k\,\|T\| \le v(T)$ for every $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$.

Determine whether
$$n(\ell_p^2) \;=\; \sup_{t\in[0,1]} \frac{|t^{p-1}-t|}{1+t^{p}}$$
holds for every $1 < p < \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The quantity $M_p = \sup_{t\in[0,1]} |t^{p-1}-t|/(1+t^p)$ is known to be a lower bound (up to a universal constant) for $n(L_p(\mu))$ and is conjectured to give the exact value for $\ell_p^2$. Work by Martín, Merí, and Popov, and subsequent work on absolute symmetric norms on the plane (arXiv:2002.07529), establishes the exact computation of $n(\ell_p^2)$ for $3/2 \le p \le 3$, confirming the conjectured formula in that range. For general $1<p<\infty$ with $p \ne 2$, the equality is not known to be fully proved.

status_evidence.title: On the numerical index of real Lp(µ)-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: M_p = max_{t∈[0,1]} |t^{p-1}-t|/(1+t^p) > 0 for every p ≠ 2; lower bound for the numerical index of real L_p(µ).
status_evidence.claim: The quantity in question is established as a lower bound for n(L_p) up to a constant.

status_evidence.title: On the numerical index of absolute symmetric norms on the plane
status_evidence.snippet: We compute the numerical index of the two-dimensional real L_p-space for 3/2 ≤ p ≤ 3.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured value of n(ℓ_p^2) is verified for 3/2 ≤ p ≤ 3, but not for all 1<p<∞.
